examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Quadric Surfaces by Completing the Square
examples.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square in the $x$ term:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}+2x+y & =0 \\ -({x}^{2}-2x)+{z}^{2}+y & =0 \\ -(x-1)^{2}+1+{z}^{2}+y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, by rearranging, we get the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}-(x-1)^{2}+1+{z}^{2}+y & =0 \\ -(x-1)^{2}+{z}^{2} & =-y-1 \\ (x-1)^{2}-{z}^{2} & =y+1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is the equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid centered at $(1, -1, 0).$

feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the equation of an elliptic cone centered at $O$ whose axis of symmetry is the $z$-axis is given by

$$
\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

Thus, an elliptic cone centered at $O$ whose axis of symmetry is the $x$**-axis** is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, our equation is an elliptic cone whose axis of symmetry is the $x$-axis and $a=1,\,b=c=2.$
